subject: Reconciling May inference-hour spike and one-off offset
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@acme-retail.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: May bill spike — need breakdown

Sergio,

Hope you’re well. Our May invoice just hit — we’re seeing a 3.8x jump in billed inference-hours vs. April (attached CSV). Finance flagged it as a retro usage issue and asked for a reconciliation/justification so we can close the month.

Can you: 1) confirm whether the consumption is genuine (traffic/model change/production rollout), 2) provide a short per-route breakdown (model names and approximate hours), and 3) propose any goodwill/one-off offset if this was an unexpected spike on Redwood’s side?

We’re on a renewal conversation and would prefer to handle this without pausing the contract. Deadline: COB Friday for our AP team.

Attachments: inference_hours_may2027.csv (CSV, 58KB)

Thanks — let me know if you want a quick sync.
Julia Park
Billing Lead, ACME Retail
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: May bill spike — need breakdown

Hi Julia — thanks for the flags and for the CSV. I pulled the raw request logs and did an initial pass. Short answers up front:

- Consumption looks legitimate (we see sustained higher QPS on the chat route tied to a campaign you launched mid-May).
- The bulk (~74%) of the increase came from two models: seq-chat-v2-large (inference-heavy) and generate-longform-1.
- That said, we also found a misconfigured client-side loop from one internal ACME service that increased prefix length and retries; that explains ~9% of the spike.

I’ve attached a condensed breakdown in the CSV (same filename you sent, with two extra columns: route and causal_tag). Quick proposal for closing this without impacting your renewal momentum:

- One-time offset: credit equivalent to 30% of the excess over baseline April usage (covers the client-side loop and shows good faith).
- Remaining excess (the campaign-driven legitimate usage) we recommend treating as a true-up charge tied to May only.

Next steps: Laura, can you draft the credit memo (amount and GL coding) and an invoice addendum? Julia, if ACME is comfortable with the split above we can prepare a DocuSign amendment to reconcile May and lock the renewal cadence.

Quoted: 
> From: Julia Park <julia@acme-retail.com>
> Subject: May bill spike — need breakdown

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Julia Park <julia@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Offset proposal and credit memo draft attached

Julia / Sergio — attaching a short offset proposal (PDF) and a draft credit memo. Key items:

- Baseline: April usage = 42,310 inference-hours. May billed = 160,354 inference-hours. Excess = 117, , 1 — (note: numbers in CSV).
- Proposed one-off offset: 30% of excess = credit for ~35,205 inference-hours (applied as an invoice credit).
- Remaining excess: billable at standard rate; we propose a payment term of Net30 and to include this as a one-time true-up invoice referencing contract ACME-2026-EXP-47.

Attachments: offset_credit_proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 24KB), credit_memo_draft.docx (DOCX, 12KB)

If ACME approves, I’ll prep the invoice and DocuSign amendment. Sergio — can you confirm the GL code we should use for the credit (we typically use 6052-credits)? Markus, flag me if accounting needs a different structure.

Laura Bennett
VP Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Julia Park <julia@acme-retail.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Retail Billing <billing@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Offset proposal and credit memo draft attached

Thanks — ACME finance reviewed the proposal and we’re comfortable with the split and the one-time offset you outlined. Two quick asks before sign: 1) please confirm the credit will be applied to the July invoice if the May true-up has already been posted; 2) include a short clause in the amendment saying this offset is a one-time courtesy and not precedent for future spikes.

We’ll sign the DocuSign once those two bullets are explicit. Appreciate the fast turnaround — looking forward to closing the renewal soon.

Julia Park
Billing Lead, ACME Retail
